# heytownhall_sso_connection (Resource)

A single sign-on connection to an OpenID Connect identity provider. An organisation can have up to five.

A new connection signs nobody in. Add one or more `heytownhall_sso_domain` resources, publish each domain's DNS record, confirm it with `heytownhall_sso_domain_verification`, and then turn the connection on with `heytownhall_sso_activation`. Enabling and enforcing sign-in are in `heytownhall_sso_activation`, not here, because they depend on a verified domain and a verified domain depends on this resource.

Register `redirect_uri` with your identity provider as the only redirect URI.

`email_claim` and `trust_unverified_email` can be changed only by an owner in the dashboard, not by a management token, so they are read-only here.

**The client secret is write-only.** The API accepts it and never returns it, so Terraform cannot see whether it was changed elsewhere. Terraform sends `client_secret` when the connection is created and whenever the value in the configuration changes. A change made to the secret in the dashboard is not detected. After an import, `client_secret` is unknown to Terraform, and the first apply sets it from the configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "okta_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "heytownhall_sso_connection" "okta" {
  name          = "Okta"
  issuer        = "https://acme.okta.com"
  client_id     = "0oa1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i9"
  client_secret = var.okta_client_secret
}

# Register this redirect URI with Okta.
output "redirect_uri" {
  value = heytownhall_sso_connection.okta.redirect_uri
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) The client id of the application registered with the identity provider.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) The application's client secret. Write-only in the API: it is never read back, so a change made outside Terraform cannot be detected. Stored in the Terraform state.
- `issuer` (String) The identity provider's issuer URL, exactly as its discovery document names it (for example `https://acme.okta.com`). It must use https. The API reads `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` when the connection is created and refuses an issuer that does not match. Changing it replaces the connection.
- `name` (String) A name for the connection, such as `Okta`.

### Read-Only

- `client_secret_updated_at` (String) When the API last stored a client secret for this connection (RFC 3339). A value later than the last apply means the secret was changed outside Terraform.
- `discovery` (Attributes) What the API read from the identity provider's discovery document when the connection was made. Read-only. It changes only when someone refreshes the connection in the dashboard or the API. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--discovery))
- `email_claim` (String) The ID token claim that holds the person's email address: `email`, `preferred_username` or `upn`. Read-only here: an owner sets it in the dashboard, because a token may not.
- `id` (String) The connection's id.
- `redirect_uri` (String) The redirect URI to register with the identity provider.
- `trust_unverified_email` (Boolean) Whether the provider's email address is accepted without an `email_verified` claim (Microsoft Entra needs it). Read-only here: an owner sets it in the dashboard, because a token may not.

<a id="nestedatt--discovery"></a>
### Nested Schema for `discovery`

Read-Only:

- `authorization_endpoint` (String) The provider's authorization endpoint.
- `jwks_uri` (String) The URL of the provider's signing keys.
- `refreshed_at` (String) When the discovery document was last read (RFC 3339).
- `token_endpoint` (String) The provider's token endpoint.
- `token_endpoint_auth_method` (String) How the API authenticates to the token endpoint: `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the connection's id. client_secret is unknown after an import; the next apply sets it from the configuration.
terraform import heytownhall_sso_connection.okta 22222222-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```
